title: Resources and Populations
seo_title: Grade 7 Population Worksheets: Limiting Factors, Carrying Capacity and Competition
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations of organisms in an ecosystem.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on resources and populations (NGSS MS-LS2-1): limiting factors, carrying capacity, competition and population graphs and data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Resources limit how big a population can grow.
key_sub: More food, water and space support larger populations. Scarce resources lead to competition and smaller populations.
body_html:
How to think about it

A population is all the members of one species in an area. Populations need resources: food, water, space, shelter and (for plants) sunlight.

When resources are plentiful, populations grow. When they are scarce, individuals compete, and fewer survive and reproduce. A resource that limits growth is a limiting factor. The largest population an area can support is its carrying capacity, so many population graphs level off.

Data and graphs show the cause and effect: a drought can cause a population to fall; extra food can cause it to rise.

Example

A drought dries a pond. What happens to the frog population?

Less water and food.

Answer: It decreases.

Example

A deer population stays near 85 for years. What is 85?

The environment supports about 85.

Answer: the carrying capacity

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a population can grow forever.
  • Thinking competition happens only between different species.
  • Ignoring how one limiting factor can control a population.

faq.a: A resource such as food, water, space or shelter that keeps a population from growing larger.
The largest population of a species that an environment can support over time with its resources.

faq.q: How does a drought affect populations?
faq.a: Less water and food means fewer organisms can survive, so populations usually decrease.

items.q: When resources are plentiful, what usually happens to a population?

items.q: What happens to individuals when resources are scarce?

items.e: Scarcity affects survival.

items.q: Can a population grow forever?
c: No. Limited resources eventually stop the growth.
items.e: Food, water and space run out.

items.q: Which is a resource plants compete for?
items.e: Plants need light, water and nutrients.

items.q: Can members of the same species compete?
c: Yes. They need the same resources.
items.e: Competition within a species is common.

items.q: What is carrying capacity?
c: the number of animals a truck can carry
the largest population an environment can support with its resources
items.e: Populations often level off near it.
